purpose: Dated, source-linked notes on what current models are good at, used to build deployment profiles and to estimate cost. Vendor pages first, third-party trackers second; benchmark versions and harnesses differ, so numbers are directional. Nothing here grants authorization: profiles.json says what a deployment may call.

openai.none: Latency-critical classification or retrieval with no chained tool calls (GPT-6 Sol and Luna only).
openai.low: Tool use, planning and multi-step decisions when speed and cost matter: data analysis, drafting, support flows.
openai.medium: Default for most workloads: agentic coding, research, spreadsheet work; planning and judgment.
openai.high: Hard reasoning, complex debugging, deep planning, high-value tasks where quality beats latency.
openai.xhigh: Deep research, long asynchronous agentic runs, security reviews and challenging coding, only when evals justify the cost.
openai.max: Maximum reasoning for the most complex problems.

anthropic.guidance: Tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models. Opus 5.5 defaults to medium (start there); Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5 default to high on the API. Escalate Sonnet -> Opus -> Fable only when evals at higher effort still fall short.

google.guidance: Gemini 3.8 Flash thinking: low for latency-critical drafting and chat, medium (default) for complex code and agents, high for deep analysis and difficult multi-step problems; `minimal` is rejected.

models.positioning: OpenAI: 'Our most capable model for the most demanding work' - complex reasoning, coding, computer use, research and document creation; the hardest end-to-end work.
best_for: scientific and research workflows (Terminal-Bench Science 0.1 leader at 68.1%)
long-horizon computer use and multi-step agent workflows
avoid_for: routine bounded edits (5x the price of Sol per token)
high-volume extraction or classification
latency-critical calls; no `none` effort

price_per_mtok.note: 2x input and 1.5x output above 272K input tokens

best_for: coding agents and computer use (DeepSWE v1.1 75.2% at high effort, above Astra's 74.1% at $0.65 vs $4.43 per task)
scientific workflows (more than doubles GPT-6 Sol on Terminal-Bench Science)
avoid_for: mechanical lookup or extraction (use Luna)
latency-critical calls; no `none` effort
architecture disputes where Astra's extra depth is justified

price_per_mtok.note: Model page unavailable on 2026-10-04 (404); OpenAI states lower cost per task than Astra. Verify on the OpenAI pricing page before budgeting.

benchmarks.Terminal-Bench Science 0.1: more than 2x GPT-6 Sol at max effort

best_for: bounded single-subsystem repairs and UI fixes with verification (high)
test-only changes, docs, backlog, asset integration
avoid_for: coupled save or rule correctness (use 6.1 Sol)
architecture and plan critique (use Astra)
mechanical lookup (Luna is 20x cheaper)

best_for: mechanical exact file or string lookup
avoid_for: implementation, diagnosis, architecture or approval (project rule and OpenAI guidance: escalate to Sol for flagship reasoning)
live or realtime sessions, audio, video, image generation (unsupported)

demanding reasoning and analysis carried to a finished document
acceptance when Opus at high effort fell short

anything outside a user-dated override in this project

models.positioning: Anthropic: 'For long-running agentic coding and knowledge work'; recommended starting point for most workloads. Finds root causes before changing anything, orchestrates subagents, matches Opus 5 quality in about half the turns. Default effort medium.
best_for: multi-hour autonomous coding, large-scale refactoring, complex systems engineering
sustained judgment: architecture, planning, plan and PRD critique
coupled save and rule correctness across systems
avoid_for: routine bounded edits where Sonnet 5.5 is 30% faster and cheaper
mechanical lookup

models.positioning: Anthropic: 'The best combination of speed and intelligence'; a faster, lower-cost complement to Opus 5.5 for well-scoped everyday tasks and bug fixing. Beats Opus 5.5 on agentic terminal coding (Terminal-Bench 4.0 70.6% vs 66.4%) and trails it by a few points elsewhere. Default effort high.
best_for: demanding bounded implementation and agentic terminal coding (high)
UI work with smoke tests and captures; design polish
routine bounded edits, docs, backlog, discovery (medium)
visual understanding of capture PNGs (project fallback visual reviewer)
avoid_for: architecture, plan critique and disputes (Opus)
coupled multi-system correctness (Opus)
independent acceptance review in this project (Opus is the authorized review profile)

models.status: ga (retirement not before 2026-10-15; Haiku 5.5 announced as coming)
models.positioning: Anthropic: 'The fastest model with near-frontier intelligence' - real-time, high-volume, cost-sensitive processing and sub-agent tasks. Not authorized in this project (CLAUDE.md: do not inherit OMC Haiku tiers).

models.positioning: Google: 'most intelligent Flash model, engineered for long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents, and complex enterprise workflows'. Text, image, audio, video and PDF input; persistent multi-step tool use; strongest third-party category is multimodal and grounded work (screenshots, documents, charts). The project's `agy` CLI profile names it `gemini-3.8-flash-high` (high thinking).
best_for: multimodal screenshot, document and chart inspection
persistent multi-step tool orchestration and long-horizon coding (DeepSWE v1.1 73.7%)
large-scale data pipelines and long context (1M)
avoid_for: terminal-heavy agentic coding on demanding harnesses (Terminal-Bench 4.0 19.1% with mini-SWE-agent vs 89.4% on Terminal-Bench 2.1; harness sensitive)
anything requiring per-call model or effort choice in this project (native override unverified; single profile)

models.status: limited release (2026-09-30: Fairwind cybersecurity partners and internal teams; paid API and AI Ultra later; no public API id)
models.positioning: Google: frontier model for complex enterprise workflows - software engineering, legal and finance knowledge work, cybersecurity defense; first or tied first on 14 of 19 published benchmarks. Not available to this project.
best_for: long-horizon software engineering and migrations (DeepSWE v1.1 77.9%, leader)
legal, finance and business automation workflows
avoid_for: terminal-driven tasks (Terminal-Bench 4.0 57.4% vs Opus 5.5 66.4%)
FrontierSWE v2 (55.0% vs Astra 65.5%)
science via shell (Terminal-Bench Science 57.6% vs Astra 68.1%)

models.positioning: Google: 'advanced intelligence, complex problem-solving skills, and powerful agentic capabilities'; still preview on 2026-10-01 and superseded in Google's roadmap by Gemini 4. Not authorized.
best_for: complex problem solving where a preview model is acceptable
avoid_for: production routing in this project (preview, no authorization)

task_guide.note: Any balanced tier at medium effort: GPT-6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (fastest), Gemini 3.8 Flash (cheapest).
Balanced tier at high effort; Sonnet 5.5 leads Terminal-Bench 4.0 (70.6%), GPT-6.1 Sol is the modern Sol.
GPT-6.1 Sol high or Claude Opus 5.5; Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra lead FrontierSWE and CursorBench.
Near-frontier correctness at the lowest price: GPT-6.1 Sol high, or Opus 5.5 for judgment-heavy acceptance.
GPT-6 Astra or Claude Opus 5.5; Fable 5.1 for hours-long research when Opus at high effort falls short.
Gemini (3.8 Flash, Argon) leads multimodal benchmarks; Claude Sonnet/Opus 5.5 read images well; vision flag required.
GPT-6 Luna, Gemini Flash-Lite or Claude Haiku 4.5: extraction and classification at the lowest price.
